title: God as Father
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: God as Father means that He reveals fatherly authority, care, compassion, discipline, provision, and covenant love. Through Christ, believers are adopted as His children and brought near to Him.
summary: God as Father means that He reveals fatherly authority, care, compassion, discipline, provision, and covenant love. Through Christ, believers are adopted as His children and brought near to Him.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the eternal Son who reveals the Father and brings believers into sonship by grace. Through Him, God’s people cry, 'Abba, Father,' by the Spirit.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture reveals God as Father in ways that display authority, love, care, holiness, and covenant faithfulness. He is not a projection of human fatherhood; true fatherhood comes from Him.

Believers know God as Father through Jesus Christ. Adoption is not earned by human worthiness. God graciously receives believers as His children through the saving work of His Son.

The Father provides, hears prayer, disciplines in love, gives identity, and grants inheritance. His fatherhood is both tender and holy. He loves His children too much to abandon them to sin.

For those whose earthly experience of fatherhood has been painful, absent, or abusive, Scripture reveals a Father who is righteous, compassionate, faithful, and safe to trust in Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people carry wounds connected to fatherhood, family, rejection, or abandonment. God as Father does not excuse earthly failure; it reveals the perfect Fatherhood from which all human fatherhood should learn.

This doctrine gives believers identity and belonging. They are not spiritual orphans, unwanted servants, or outsiders trying to earn a place. In Christ, they are children of God.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to God as Father through Christ. Pray with reverence and trust, receive His discipline as love, rest in your adoption, and treat other believers as family. Let the Father’s love heal false views of worth, belonging, and identity.
